source.implementation_note: veinnet_runtime.preprocessing.demographics.demographics_transform() is a DIRECT IMPLEMENTATION of this manifest's feature_schema.contract and train_normalization stats. It is NOT training source code copied verbatim from the repository -- no equivalent single-reading (age, sex) -> vector transform exists upstream; gate7_max30102_personaldelta/demographics.py only re-validates the precomputed per-cohort .npy arrays against this same manifest hash. The runtime function was written fresh from the documented contract and approved for inclusion 2026-09-01.

transform.age_z: 0.0 if age is missing else (age - train_age_mean) / train_age_std
transform.is_female: 1.0 only if sex == canonical_female ('F'); 0.0 for canonical male ('M') or missing/unknown

canonicalization_policy: The frozen transform accepts only the exact strings 'F', 'M', or None for sex -- it performs no case-folding or synonym mapping (e.g. 'female', 'male', 'f', 'm' are all rejected with ValueError). A separate, explicitly documented adapter -- outside this frozen module -- may canonicalize external representations before calling demographics_transform().

input_validation_added_for_runtime_safet.age_type: must be int or float (not bool) or None; TypeError otherwise
input_validation_added_for_runtime_safet.age_finite: must be finite (not NaN/inf) when provided; ValueError otherwise
input_validation_added_for_runtime_safet.age_plausible_range: [0, 130] years when provided; ValueError otherwise -- this bound is a runtime input-validation guard, NOT part of the frozen manifest transform math, added because the manifest contract only specifies the transform for already-plausible ages
input_validation_added_for_runtime_safet.sex_type: must be exactly 'F', 'M', or None; ValueError otherwise (see canonicalization_policy)

output_contract.scalar: numpy.float32 array, shape (4,), order [age_z, is_female, age_missing, sex_missing]
output_contract.batch: veinnet_runtime.preprocessing.demographics.demographics_transform_batch(rows) stacks demographics_transform() per row deterministically; numpy.float32 array, shape (len(rows), 4)
